facts.raw_span: A female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

was admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
Seventeen days after her last day of chemotherapy, while neutropenic, she became febrile
Patient had an indwelling catheter
Several vesicles with an erythematous base were observed on the lower back and left thigh
Hematoxylin-eosin stain showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa
Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods in the necrotic epidermis and dermis
Periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for herpes simplex virus (HSV) and varicella zoster virus (VZV) were negative
CT scan with contrast of thorax and brain showed lesions in the liver and brain

concepts.why: The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa on hematoxylin-eosin stain and gram-variable rods on Gram stain, along with negative PCR testing for HSV and VZV, supports the diagnosis of Bacillus cereus infection.

The patient's neutropenic state, indwelling catheter, and presence of vesicles with an erythematous base are consistent with Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, a common cause of infection in immunocompromised patients.

The presence of filamentous bacilli with septa on hematoxylin-eosin stain and gram-variable rods on Gram stain, along with lesions in the liver and brain on CT scan, are consistent with Nocardia infection, which can cause disseminated disease in immunocompromised patients.

The negative result of Periodic acid-Schiff staining for fungal elements, combined with the presence of gram-variable rods, points towards a bacterial infection, which is consistent with Bacillus cereus infection.

rationales.F04: Indwelling catheter increases risk of various infections, but is not specific to Bacillus cereus or Nocardia, and slightly more associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa.
rationales.F05: Vesicles with an erythematous base could be indicative of Bacillus cereus infection, which is known to cause cutaneous lesions.
rationales.F06: Filamentous bacilli with septa are characteristic of Bacillus cereus and Nocardia infections, strongly suggesting these diagnoses.
rationales.F07: Gram-variable rods are consistent with Bacillus cereus and Nocardia, supporting these diagnoses.
rationales.F08: Negative fungal staining helps to rule out fungal infections, making bacterial infections like Nocardia more likely.
rationales.F10: Disseminated lesions in liver and brain are consistent with Nocardia infection, which can disseminate in immunocompromised patients.
